**The Premier League match between Ipswich Town (home) and Nottingham Forest was scheduled for March 15, 2025 (around Matchweek 29 of the 2024/25 season), at Portman Road.**[[1]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/401878661/ipswich-town-nottingham-forest)[[2]](https://www.whoscored.com/articles/0n_8RFmFmkKBszGcjtr_Mg/show/ipswich-vs-nottingham-forest-prediction-team-news-predicted-lineups-where-to-watch-premier-league)

All information below draws exclusively from sources and data published before March 15, 2025. Any post-match results or later developments have been ignored. ### Head-to-Head History
Historical meetings (primarily from Championship and earlier eras, with limited recent Premier League context as both clubs were promoted around the same time):
- Across ~29–39 meetings since the early 2000s (exact counts vary by source), Ipswich won around 6–9, with Nottingham Forest securing more victories (often 15+ in broader tallies) and roughly 10 draws. Average goals per game hovered near 2.8–3.[[3]](https://m.aiscore.com/head-to-head/soccer-ipswich-town-vs-nottingham-forest)[[4]](https://www.soccerpunter.com/h2h/Ipswich-Town-vs-Nottingham-Forest/116/63/)[[5]](https://www.fctables.com/h2h/ipswich/nottingham-forest/)
- Notable past results include Ipswich wins like a 4-2 home victory in December 2017 (Championship) and mixed outcomes in 2017–18 fixtures.[[6]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/ipswich-town/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Nottingham%20Forest/)
- In major competitions or high-stakes contexts, Forest generally held a slight edge in recent decades, though direct Premier League H2H was minimal pre-2024/25 due to league placements. Recent prior meetings in 2024/25 (pre-March) were limited; one noted FA Cup fifth-round clash occurred on or around March 3, 2025, but details are not used here beyond noting it as a separate competition.[[7]](https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/732566/ipswich-town-nottingham-forest)

### Recent Form and League Context (Pre-March 15, 2025)
- **Ipswich Town**: Newly promoted side struggling in the lower half of the Premier League table (around 18th place in previews). They recorded a poor overall 2024/25 record of roughly 4 wins, 10 draws, and 24 losses across the season to that point (22 points, 0.58 PPG), with particularly weak home form (1-4-14).[[8]](https://fbref.com/en/squads/b74092de/2024-2025/matchlogs/c9/schedule/Ipswich-Town-Scores-and-Fixtures-Premier-League)[[2]](https://www.whoscored.com/articles/0n_8RFmFmkKBszGcjtr_Mg/show/ipswich-vs-nottingham-forest-prediction-team-news-predicted-lineups-where-to-watch-premier-league)
- **Nottingham Forest**: Performing strongly, sitting as high as 3rd in previews and pushing for an unlikely top-four or European finish. They showed good momentum with winning streaks noted earlier in the season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Nottingham_Forest_F.C._season)[[2]](https://www.whoscored.com/articles/0n_8RFmFmkKBszGcjtr_Mg/show/ipswich-vs-nottingham-forest-prediction-team-news-predicted-lineups-where-to-watch-premier-league)

Ipswich faced a tough home challenge against a higher-placed, in-form opponent. ### Injuries, Suspensions, and Team News
Specific pre-match injury updates for the March 15 fixture were not detailed in widely available previews, but general context included:
- Ipswich’s George Hirst (knee) had been sidelined for extended periods (missing ~9 matches earlier) and was returning to limited minutes in early 2025.[[10]](https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/george-hirst-2-player)
- Nottingham Forest had occasional mentions of squad concerns in broader 2024/25 coverage, though no standout key-player absences were flagged in immediate previews. Rotational considerations (e.g., for cup games) were noted for managers like Kieran McKenna (Ipswich).[[11]](https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c8x441lyk9go)

No major suspensions were prominently highlighted in available pre-match material. ### Travel, Fatigue, Venue, and Home Advantage
- **Travel/fatigue**: Both clubs are based in England (Ipswich in Suffolk, Forest in Nottinghamshire). The approximate driving distance is ~140–160 miles, involving a relatively straightforward trip unlikely to cause significant fatigue for a domestic league game. - **Venue conditions**: Portman Road is a standard Premier League stadium with no notable altitude or extreme climate issues. Pitch conditions were not flagged as unusual in previews. - **Crowd/home advantage**: Ipswich benefited from home support at Portman Road, a factor for promoted sides, though Forest’s strong away form and higher league position were expected to mitigate this. No specific attendance or atmosphere notes were prominent pre-match. ### Other Notable Storylines
- This was a matchup of two recently promoted sides (both from the 2023/24 Championship), with Ipswich under Kieran McKenna aiming to consolidate and Forest (under Nuno Espírito Santo or successor) exceeding expectations with a high league position. - Previews framed it as a difficult test for struggling Ipswich against a confident, higher-placed Forest side.[[12]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/premier-league/ipswich-town-vs-nottingham-forest_game_200422.html)[[2]](https://www.whoscored.com/articles/0n_8RFmFmkKBszGcjtr_Mg/show/ipswich-vs-nottingham-forest-prediction-team-news-predicted-lineups-where-to-watch-premier-league)
- Broader context included Ipswich’s overall relegation battle and Forest’s push for European spots. This covers the key contextual factors available from pre-March 15, 2025 sources.

analysis.reasoning: The research notes present a stark contrast in performance and league standing between the two teams. Ipswich Town is explicitly described as a 'struggling' newly promoted side in the relegation zone, particularly highlighted by their abysmal home record of 1 win, 4 draws, and 14 losses. Conversely, Nottingham Forest is performing exceptionally well, sitting as high as 3rd in the league and pushing for European qualification. While Ipswich is at home, the notes explicitly state that Forest's strong away form and higher league position are expected to 'mitigate' this advantage. The historical head-to-head also leans towards Forest. Given the extreme disparity in recent form, league position, and Ipswich's specific home struggles, a substantial adjustment favoring Nottingham Forest is well-justified and supported by multiple strong factors.
